step_by_step_reasoning: The analysis began by identifying all distinct visual elements on the whiteboard, including AWS service icons (ECS, Lambda, DynamoDB, RDS PostgreSQL, SNS) and conceptual boxes ('NON-PROD', 'PROD'). The 'Service Teams' icon was identified as an external actor. Each identified visual component was mapped to a Cloudscape node type, ensuring strict adherence to AWS service names and semantic ontology for external actors. For instance, 'Service Teams' was mapped to 'UserCompanyDeveloper' and 'NON-PROD' and 'PROD' were mapped to 'UserCompanyInternalPlatform' as they represent internal bank environments/accounts. The transcript was then used to understand the data flow, purpose of each service, and the sequence of operations (build event capture, promotion request/validation, successful promotion). Edges were drawn based on explicit visual arrows on the whiteboard and corroborated by the transcript to establish data flow, sequence, and type (data/meta). Ambiguous visual lines (e.g., ECS to NON-PROD feedback loop) were omitted if not explicitly described as a data flow in the transcript. The 'x25' next to Lambda was noted as a quantity detail for the logical Lambda service. SQS and a Lambda within PROD were mentioned in the transcript but not visually drawn as distinct icons, so they were not included as separate nodes, adhering to the 'visual-first' and 'strictly parsimonious' rules. Flow IDs and sequence numbers were assigned to trace the end-to-end process from external actors inwards.

graph.name: NAB Compliance Framework for Cloud Workloads
graph.notes: This architecture by National Australia Bank (NAB) outlines a compliance framework to automate workload migration to AWS. It ensures rapid, compliant deployment by validating build events against defined standards before promotion to production, leveraging serverless and managed database services.

nodes.name: Service Teams
nodes.notes: NAB service teams, customers of the platform, running pipelines in non-production accounts.

nodes.name: NON-PROD Account
nodes.notes: Non-production environment where service teams run their pipelines and initiate promotion requests.

nodes.name: Kong on ECS
nodes.notes: Runs Kong gateway to publish API endpoints for event ingestion and promotion requests.

nodes.name: Lambda Functions
nodes.notes: Collection of Lambda functions (x25) to capture events, execute assessments, and handle API calls.

nodes.name: Build Event Store
nodes.notes: Stores captured build events from pipelines as key-value pairs for compliance validation.

nodes.name: Compliance Framework RDS PostgreSQL
nodes.notes: Stores the relational compliance framework (standards, controls, how to meet them) in PostgreSQL.

nodes.name: Promotion Notification SNS
nodes.notes: Used to securely send promotion notifications to production accounts with fan-out capabilities.

nodes.name: PROD Account
nodes.notes: Production environment where validated deployments occur, triggered by SNS notifications and managed by internal deployment tools.

edges.notes: Service teams run pipelines within their non-production accounts.
Pipelines in non-production account send build events to Kong running on ECS.
Kong publishes endpoints, routing build events to Lambda.
Lambda captures build events and stores them in DynamoDB.
Service teams make an API call to promote from non-production account.
Promote API call goes through Kong on ECS.
Kong routes promote API call to Lambda.
Lambda retrieves build event data from DynamoDB for validation.
Lambda queries RDS PostgreSQL for compliance framework definitions.
Compliance framework data returned to Lambda for assessment execution.
Upon successful compliance assessment, Lambda publishes a promotion notification to SNS.
SNS fans out promotion notification to the production account, triggering deployment logic.
Logical flow of artifacts/code promotion from non-production to production environment.
